blindSummary:
This state/province recorded 5 killings of trans people (trans women and people of a local trans-feminine identity category) in 2025, the same count as two other states; it also recorded 5 in 2024, so the toll is persistent rather than a one-year spike. Against a population of ~7.1 million the 2025 rate is about 0.70 per million per year, roughly double the national figure (~0.38). It is among the poorest states in the federation, and the dossier's victim profile - young, black, poor, and drawn from the country's poorest broad region - maps directly onto its demographics, indicating the killings track structural exposure rather than incidental misfortune.

No local ordinance or legal finding was identified; the profile rests on the sustained killing counts. For scale, the two highest-count states recorded 8 killings each in the same year.
blindSourceSummaries: The national trans-murder monitoring association's ninth annual dossier (released 26 Jan 2026, reported by a broadcast outlet): the country recorded 80 murders of trans people in 2025, 34% down on 2024 but with at least 75 attempted homicides and crimes marked by excessive violence; 2025 per-state counts in descending order - 8, 8, 7, 7, 5, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, 4, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2; 1,261 murders over 2017-2025 (avg 140/year); 97% of victims were trans women (including a local trans-feminine identity category), over half aged 18-29, 70% black among racially-identified cases; 67.5% of killings happened in interior cities rather than capitals, where monitoring, denunciation and access to public policies are harder; the country has led the global ranking since 2008. Places this state/province in the 5-killings band for 2025.

Coverage of the association's 2024 dossier (27 Jan 2025): the country led global trans-murder tallies for the 16th consecutive year with 122 killings in 2024, a 16% fall on 2023; the victim profile was predominantly young, black, poor and from the country's poorest broad region, with the population's life expectancy cited at about 35 years; most murders happen in public places, at night, with extreme cruelty; authorities rarely register victims' gender identity, degrading official data; the 2024 state-by-state table places this state/province at 5 killings, alongside one other state at 5 and others at 2, 6 and 8; the association's president demands effective public policies and honest statistics. Gives this state/province's 2024 count, plus the victim-profile and life-expectancy findings.
